description: Create a monitor for a routine. Use cron, tz and grace_sec for a schedule, or interval_sec for a fixed check-in interval. Set max_duration_sec to detect an open run that exceeds its time limit. Read billing before a paid option. A charged request returns HTTP 402. This response is the only one that shows the monitor's `token` and the `templates` — keep them. The second monitor, or an interval below the free minimum, answers **402 with `accepts[]`**: pay and repeat. A miss alerts at most once per 24h — or per `alert_repeat_sec`, or per interval, whichever is longer. Send `cron`+`tz`+`grace_sec` instead of `interval_sec` for a real schedule: a 03:00 backup is late at 03:01:30, not 24 hours later. `max_duration_sec` catches the other failure: a run that starts and hangs, which plain silence detection only notices at the next scheduled time.

alert_repeat_sec.description: gap before the same incident alerts again, 3600..2592000; null keeps the 86400 default

alert_to.description: E-mail to alert on a miss; without it, the account is alerted.

alert_url.description: Public HTTPS URL that receives a POST on a miss (Slack Incoming, Discord, n8n).

grace_sec.description: tolerance after the scheduled time, default 90, min 30

interval_sec.description: Tolerated silence, in seconds. Below the free minimum, it costs.

max_duration_sec.description: ceiling for an open run in seconds, 60..86400; null or 0 turns it off

name.description: how you will recognise the routine in an alert; required, trimmed, max 80 chars, punctuation alone is rejected

paused_until.description: maintenance window end (UTC ISO), max 30 days ahead

tags.description: up to 8 tags to group the monitor; lower-cased, [a-z0-9._-], max 32 chars each

tz.description: IANA time zone for cron, default UTC
